name: Charlie Health IOP
one_liner: Virtual intensive outpatient program (IOP): about 9–12 hours a week of group, individual and family therapy by video, ages 8–64.
best_for: Kids, teens and adults whose symptoms need more than one therapy session a week but not a hospital stay
People stepping down from inpatient or residential treatment
Families who want family therapy built into treatment
People with commercial insurance, or Medicaid in a state where Charlie Health takes it
not_for: Anyone in crisis or at immediate risk: call 911, or call or text 988
People who need 24-hour supervision, detox or hospitalization
People who can't commit about 9+ hours a week for several weeks (insurers may stop covering below that)
People looking for occasional or weekly therapy only
short_description: Virtual intensive outpatient program (IOP) for serious mental health or substance use needs: more than weekly therapy, less than residential.
long_description: Charlie Health runs a virtual intensive outpatient program (IOP), a level of care between weekly outpatient therapy and residential or inpatient treatment. Its site describes 10+ hours of care a week, typically across three days, made up of three group sessions, one individual session and one family session a week, with medication management if needed; programs typically last 6 to 12 weeks. It serves ages 8 to 64 (substance use care from 13) in about 40 states and works with 600+ insurance plans, plus Medicaid in some states. It publishes no self-pay rate. Charlie Health staff have published several uncontrolled quality-improvement analyses of their own patients in JMIR Formative Research; there are no randomized trials of the program.
patient_summary: Charlie Health is a step above weekly therapy: you join a virtual intensive outpatient program with about three group sessions a week plus individual and family therapy, usually for several weeks, from home by video. You start with a call to admissions, who check whether your insurance covers it; most patients use commercial insurance or Medicaid in some states, and self-pay is offered only in some states by estimate.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; no published self-pay rate
pricing.notes: Works with 600+ insurance plans and Medicaid in states where IOP is covered. Self-pay offered only in select states, with payment plans; ask admissions for an estimate. Coverage may stop if attendance drops below about 9 hours a week.

privacy.notes: Policy says it discloses some personal information to advertising partners for targeted advertising (opt-out form offered) while also saying it does not sell it; deletion rights depend on your state. Treatment records fall under its HIPAA notice and 42 CFR Part 2.

seo.title: Charlie Health: Virtual IOP for Teens & Young Adults
seo.meta_description: Charlie Health provides virtual intensive outpatient programs (IOP) for teens and young adults with serious mental health needs, often covered by insurance.

faqs.a: Charlie Health IOP (Intensive Outpatient Program) provides 9-15 hours per week of virtual group therapy, individual therapy, and family sessions for teens and young adults. It's more intensive than weekly therapy but allows you to stay home and continue school/work. Programs typically last 8-12 weeks.

faqs.q: Is Charlie Health covered by insurance?
faqs.a: Most commercial insurance covers Charlie Health IOP/PHP, and many families pay $0-50 per session. Charlie Health verifies benefits and handles insurance billing. Medicaid coverage varies by state. They also offer self-pay options for those without coverage.

faqs.q: What ages does Charlie Health treat?
faqs.a: Charlie Health treats adolescents, teens, and young adults ages 11-30. Programs are tailored to developmental stages with separate groups for middle schoolers, high schoolers, and young adults. Family involvement is a core component of treatment.

faqs.q: What conditions does Charlie Health treat?
faqs.a: Charlie Health treats depression, anxiety, trauma/PTSD, suicidal ideation, self-harm, eating disorders, substance use, and personality disorders. The IOP level is appropriate for moderate-severe symptoms not requiring 24-hour supervision.

clinical_trials.study: Outcomes for youth with public vs private insurance in Charlie Health's virtual IOP

citation.authors: Gliske K, Berry KR, Ballard J, Evans-Chase M, Solomon PL, Fenkel C
citation.title: Mental Health Outcomes for Youths With Public Versus Private Health Insurance Attending a Telehealth Intensive Outpatient Program: Quality Improvement Analysis

clinical_trials.outcome: Youth on public and private insurance engaged at similar rates and had similar improvements in depression, suicidality and self-harm scores; no control group; company-funded.

primary_uses: Intensive outpatient care for depression, anxiety and trauma
Support after self-harm or suicidal thoughts when hospitalization isn't needed
Step-down care after inpatient or residential treatment
Family therapy alongside group and individual therapy
